**Can I stream my DJI drone to TikTok and YouTube at the same time?** Yes. Add both as destinations and press START LIVE. Because both share one orientation, choose the one that suits your main audience.

**Do I need a restream service?** No. DJI Live Bridge does the multistreaming on your own computer, for free; it only needs enough upload bandwidth.

**What happens if one platform drops?** Only that destination shows Connection failed. The others keep streaming.

**Does each extra platform need more CPU?** Hardly. The picture is encoded once and the same data is sent to every destination.

**Does multistream work in OBS mode?** No. Several destinations are a feature of direct streaming; in OBS mode, OBS decides where the stream goes.

## DJI Live Bridge vs Restream: which one for your drone?
Source: https://tanerozel.github.io/dji-live-bridge/blog/dji-live-bridge-vs-restream/ (updated 2026-10-03)

Both get one drone feed onto several platforms. Restream does it in the cloud: DJI Fly streams to Restream's servers, which forward the video. DJI Live Bridge does it on your own computer: DJI Fly streams over your local network to the app, which sends it to each platform. Which is better depends on where you fly and what you pay for.

- Restream is a cloud service: no computer in the field, one upload, but a subscription for more than the basics.
- Restream's free plan (October 2026): 2 channels, Restream branding on the stream, no custom RTMP destinations; Standard is $19 a month.
- DJI Live Bridge is free and open source: no watermark, no channel limit, the video stays on your own computer.
- DJI Live Bridge reshapes the drone picture into vertical 1080×1920 for Instagram and TikTok and adds a virtual camera for TikTok LIVE Studio.
- You can also combine them: add Restream as a custom RTMP destination in DJI Live Bridge.

### Two different approaches
- Restream (cloud): DJI Fly → internet → Restream → each platform. The controller needs internet; the computer is optional.
- DJI Live Bridge (local): DJI Fly → local Wi-Fi → your Mac or PC → each platform. The computer needs internet; the controller only needs the local network.
That single difference explains most of the comparison: the cloud saves your upload bandwidth and a computer, the local app saves a subscription and keeps the video in your hands.

### Side by side
|  | DJI Live Bridge | Restream |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Price | Free, open source | Free plan; paid from $19/month (Standard) |
| Watermark | None | Restream branding on the free plan |
| Destinations | As many as your upload allows | 2 on free, 3 on Standard, more on higher plans |
| Custom RTMP destinations | Yes | Not on the free plan |
| Instagram from DJI Fly | Yes, the app sends RTMPS | Depends on how your plan connects Instagram |
| Vertical 1080×1920 with blurred fill | Built in | Not a drone feature; the stream goes out as sent |
| Virtual camera (TikTok LIVE Studio, OBS, Zoom) | Built in | No |
| Computer in the field | Needed (or Stream My Drone on Android) | Not needed |
| Upload used | Once per destination | Once in total |
| Chat and analytics | No | Yes |
| Where the video goes | Only to your destinations | Through Restream's servers |
Restream's plans are from its pricing page in October 2026 and can change; check the current page before deciding.

### When Restream is the better choice
- You want to stream straight from the controller with no computer or second phone.
- Your upload is slow and you need many destinations: the cloud sends one upload to all of them.
- You want combined chat, analytics or team features across platforms.

### When DJI Live Bridge is the better choice
- You do not want a monthly bill or a watermark on your broadcast.
- You stream to Instagram or TikTok and want a proper vertical picture, not a landscape strip.
- You want to go live on TikTok without a stream key, through TikTok LIVE Studio and the built-in virtual camera.
- The footage is sensitive — a client site, an inspection — and should not pass through a third party.
- You want a preview, recording and diagnostics on a big screen next to you.
Get it for macOS or Windows; the setup is in the DJI Fly RTMP guide.

### Using both together
If you already pay for Restream, keep the vertical picture and the preview from DJI Live Bridge and let Restream handle the fan-out:
1. **Copy Restream's RTMP details** In Restream, find the RTMP server URL and stream key for your encoder.
2. **Add a Custom RTMP destination** In DJI Live Bridge, add a custom destination with that URL and key.
3. **Go live** Send the drone to the app from DJI Fly and press START LIVE; Restream forwards it to your channels.

### FAQ
**Is DJI Live Bridge a free alternative to Restream?** For drone streaming, yes: it sends one DJI Fly feed to several platforms at no cost and without a watermark. It runs on your computer instead of in the cloud, so the computer's upload carries every destination.

**Does Restream add a watermark?** On the free plan, Restream adds its branding to the stream (October 2026). Paid plans remove it.

**Can I use DJI Live Bridge and Restream together?** Yes. Add Restream as a custom RTMP destination in DJI Live Bridge.

**Which one works without a computer?** Restream, because DJI Fly can stream to it directly over the internet. For DJI Live Bridge you need a computer, or the Android app Stream My Drone when you fly with a DJI RC 2.

## Stream a DJI drone without setting up NGINX and OBS
Source: https://tanerozel.github.io/dji-live-bridge/blog/dji-drone-to-obs-without-nginx/ (updated 2026-10-03)

Search for how to get a DJI drone into OBS and most guides start the same way: install an NGINX RTMP server, edit its config, open the firewall, point DJI Fly at it and pull the stream into OBS as a media source. It works, but it is a small server project. DJI Live Bridge puts the RTMP server, the preview, the encoding and the platform outputs in one app — and can still hand the picture to OBS when you want it.

- The classic recipe is DJI Fly → NGINX with the RTMP module → OBS media source → one platform.
- It means installing a server, editing nginx.conf, allowing port 1935 and building a scene by hand.
- Several platforms at once needs an OBS plugin or a cloud service; a vertical canvas needs more setup.
- DJI Live Bridge receives DJI Fly directly and streams to several platforms, vertical or horizontal, with nothing else installed.
- If you want OBS anyway, Prepare OBS scene builds a DJI LIVE scene with the drone feed for you.

### The usual NGINX + OBS recipe
1. **Install an RTMP server** NGINX with the RTMP module (on Windows often a prebuilt bundle), or another RTMP server.
2. **Edit the configuration** Add an rtmp block with an application such as live to nginx.conf and start the server.
3. **Open the firewall** Allow incoming connections on port 1935 and find the computer's local address.
4. **Point DJI Fly at it** Enter something like rtmp://192.168.1.20/live/drone under Live Streaming Platforms → RTMP.
5. **Pull it into OBS** Add a Media Source with the same address, size it on the canvas, then set OBS's stream URL and key for your platform.
After that, every change is manual: a new network means a new address, a second platform means a plugin or a relay service, and a vertical stream means a second canvas or a separate profile.

### What DJI Live Bridge replaces
| Task | NGINX + OBS | DJI Live Bridge |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RTMP server for DJI Fly | Install and configure NGINX | Built in; the address is shown with a QR code |
| Preview of the drone | OBS media source | Built in, with resolution and bitrate |
| Several platforms at once | Plugin or cloud service | Built in |
| Instagram (RTMPS) | OBS can send RTMPS to one destination | Built in, alongside the others |
| Vertical 1080×1920 | Build a vertical canvas | One switch, with a blurred fill |
| TikTok without a stream key | OBS Virtual Camera + LIVE Studio | Built-in virtual camera |
| Stream keys | In OBS's settings | In the system's credential vault |

### The one-app setup
1. **Install DJI Live Bridge** Download it for macOS or Windows; FFmpeg and the media server are inside.
2. **Copy the address into DJI Fly** The app shows an address like rtmp://192.168.1.20:1935/drone. Enter it in DJI Fly under GO FLY → ••• → Transmission → Live Streaming Platforms → RTMP.
3. **Add your platforms** Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Facebook, Twitch, Kick or any RTMP server, each with its URL and key.
4. **Press START LIVE** The picture is encoded once and sent to every enabled destination.

### When you still want OBS
OBS is unbeatable for scenes, overlays and transitions. DJI Live Bridge does not replace that — it replaces the NGINX part. Enable OBS WebSocket (Tools → WebSocket Server Settings), connect it in the app's Advanced tab and press Prepare OBS scene: the app creates a scene named DJI LIVE with the drone feed already in it, sized to a horizontal or vertical canvas.
For calls in Zoom, Meet or Teams through OBS Virtual Camera, see the webcam guide.

### FAQ
**Do I need NGINX to stream a DJI drone to OBS?** No. DJI Live Bridge contains its own RTMP server; with Prepare OBS scene it also puts the drone feed into OBS without NGINX.

**Do I need OBS to stream a DJI drone?** No. DJI Live Bridge streams to Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and other platforms directly. OBS is optional for scenes and overlays.

**Is the NGINX method worse?** It works and is flexible, but you maintain a server, a config file and an OBS scene yourself, and multistreaming or vertical video need extra steps.

**What does DJI Live Bridge cost?** Nothing. It is free and open source under the MIT licence.
